prompt: $\dfrac{1+2+3+4}{1\times2\times5}$ is equal to

solutions.title: Compute
solutions.body:
Numerator $1+2+3+4=10$, denominator $1\times2\times5=10$. The fraction is $1$.

**Answer: (B) 1**

prompt: Noni knits a blanket. She uses 2 colours and follows the pattern as shown. The fraction of the blanket knitted in the darker shade is

solutions.title: Count triangles
solutions.body:
Each small square is split into 2 triangles, giving $20\times2=40$ triangles, of which 10 are dark. The fraction is $\frac{10}{40}=\frac14$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac14$**

solutions.title: Repeating block
solutions.body:
The pattern is made of blocks of 2 squares side by side (4 triangles); each block has exactly 1 dark triangle, so $\frac14$ of the blanket is dark.

**Answer: (E) $\frac14$**

prompt: If two dice are rolled, which total is most likely?

solutions.title: Count ways
solutions.body:
Number of ways to get totals 2 to 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. The total 7 can be made in 6 ways: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1), more than any other.

**Answer: (A) 7**

prompt: For long distance telephone calls, Telkom charges 30.9 cents per metering unit of 13.6 seconds. The cost of a 3 minute long distance call to the nearest rand is

solutions.title: Estimate the units
solutions.body:
3 minutes is 180 seconds, and $180\div13.6\approx13$ units. $13\times30.9\approx 400$ cents, which is about R4.

**Answer: (E) R4.00**

prompt: A rectangular carpet has a perimeter of 16 m and area $15\text{ m}^2$. The lengths of the sides of the carpet in metres are

solutions.title: Sum and product
solutions.body:
Half the perimeter is 8, so the sides add up to 8 and multiply to 15. $3+5=8$ and $3\times5=15$.

**Answer: (E) 5 and 3**

solutions.title: Test the options
solutions.body:
Only the pair 5 and 3 has both sum 8 and product 15 ($10+6$, $15+1$, $8+2$, $7.5+2$ all have the wrong sum).

**Answer: (E) 5 and 3**

prompt: A five sided regular polygon is drawn with dotted diagonal lines as shown from one vertex to the other vertices. If a regular polygon has 50 sides and diagonals are drawn from one vertex to the other vertices, how many diagonals are there?

solutions.title: Exclude the neighbours
solutions.body:
From one vertex there are 49 other vertices. Two of them are neighbours (joined by sides, not diagonals), so there are $49-2=47$ diagonals. (Check for the pentagon: $5-3=2$.)

**Answer: (B) 47**

prompt: Suppose there are 20 million learners attending schools in South Africa of which ten percent are in Grades 8 and 9. Each learner in Grade 8 and 9 must receive a Mathematics text book costing R30, a set of language books costing R70, a science text book costing R40 and a history book at R60. What is the total cost for the Department of Education if they have to purchase all these text books?

solutions.title: Multiply
solutions.body:
Grade 8 and 9 learners: $10\%$ of 20 million $=2$ million. Cost per learner: $30+70+40+60=\text{R}200$. Total $2\,000\,000\times200=\text{R}400\,000\,000$, i.e. R400 million.

**Answer: (D) R400 million**

prompt: Approximately how far away did the lightning strike if I heard the sound of the thunder 12 seconds after I saw the lightning? (Let the speed of sound be about 332 m/s.)

solutions.title: Distance = speed times time
solutions.body:
$12\times332=3984$ m, which is about 4 km (the light arrives almost instantly).

**Answer: (E) 4 km**

prompt: Dr Maharaj travels 45 000 km in his car. During that time he changes the tyres, including the spare, regularly so that at the end of the 45 000 km journey each tyre has the same amount of wear. How many kilometres of wear does each tyre have?

solutions.title: Share the wear
solutions.body:
Four tyres are on the car at any time, so the total tyre-kilometres is $4\times45\,000=180\,000$. This is shared equally by 5 tyres: $180\,000\div5=36\,000$ km each.

**Answer: (C) 36 000**

solutions.title: Fraction
solutions.body:
Each tyre is on the car for $\frac45$ of the time, so $\frac45\times45\,000=36\,000$ km.

**Answer: (C) 36 000**

prompt: Anusha has 3 questions correct in section A of this paper and 7 correct in section B. She hopes to score 60% to advance to the next round. The least number of questions she must get right in section C is

solutions.title: Count marks
solutions.body:
The paper has 5 questions of 3 marks, 10 of 5 marks and 5 of 7 marks, total $15+50+35=100$ marks, so she needs 60 marks. She has $3\times3+7\times5=44$, so needs 16 more. Two questions in section C give only 14, three give 21, so the least number is 3.

**Answer: (C) 3**

prompt: Circle, centre O, has triangles AOC and COB drawn inside it. AOB is a straight line. If $\angle OBC=58^\circ$ then the size of $\angle OCA$ (marked $y$) is

solutions.title: Isosceles triangles
solutions.body:
$OB=OC$ so $\angle OCB=58^\circ$. $OA=OC$, so $\angle OAC=\angle OCA=y$. In triangle ABC the angles sum to $180^\circ$: $y+58+y+58=180$, so $2y=64$ and $y=32^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $32^\circ$**

solutions.title: Angle in a semicircle
solutions.body:
AB is a diameter, so $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. Then $\angle ACO=90^\circ-\angle OCB=90^\circ-58^\circ=32^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $32^\circ$**

prompt: The cost of 2 pens and 3 rulers is R1.90. If a pen costs 20 cents more than a ruler, then the cost of 2 rulers and 3 pens in rand is

solutions.title: Equations
solutions.body:
Let a ruler cost $y$ cents; a pen costs $y+20$. $2(y+20)+3y=190$, so $5y=150$, $y=30$, pen $=50$. Then $2\times30+3\times50=210$ cents $=$ R2.10.

**Answer: (A) 2.10**

solutions.title: Compare
solutions.body:
Going from 2 pens + 3 rulers to 3 pens + 2 rulers replaces one ruler by one pen, which costs 20 cents more: $190+20=210$ cents.

**Answer: (A) 2.10**

prompt: In the $20^{\text{th}}$ century (1901 – 2000), how many years are divisible by 6?

solutions.title: List
solutions.body:
The first multiple of 6 in the range is $1902=6\times317$ and the last is $1998=6\times333$. That is $333-317+1=17$ years.

**Answer: (C) 17**

prompt: A birthday present is tied with ribbon as shown. The bow, knots and ends used 47 cm of ribbon. The total length of the ribbon used, in metres, is

solutions.title: Add the parts
solutions.body:
The ribbon goes round the box twice along the length (20 cm) and the width (15 cm) and four times along the height (10 cm): $2\times20+2\times15+4\times10=40+30+40=110$ cm. Plus 47 cm for the bow gives $157$ cm $=1.57$ m.

**Answer: (A) 1.57**

prompt: A target consists of rings of width 1 cm. The radius of the inner black circle is 1 cm. Determine how many times the area of the outer black ring is bigger than the area of the inner black circle.

solutions.title: Areas
solutions.body:
The outer black ring has outer radius 3 cm and inner radius 2 cm: area $\pi(9-4)=5\pi$. The inner circle has area $\pi$. The ratio is 5.

**Answer: (E) 5**

prompt:
In this addition, different letters stand for different digits, but each letter represents the same digit each time it appears. If the letter O stands for 7, what digit must U represent?

$$\begin{array}{r} TWO\\ +\ TWO\\ \hline FOUR\end{array}$$

solutions.title: Column by column
solutions.body:
Units: $O+O=14$ gives $R=4$ with a carry of 1. Thousands: $F=1$ (a carry from the hundreds). Hundreds: $T+T+\text{carry}$ gives a two-digit number starting $1O=17$, so $T=8$ (with carry 1 from the tens, $8+8+1=17$). Tens: $W+W+1=10+U$, so $W\ge5$. $W=5$ gives $U=1=F$, $W=7$ and $W=8$ clash with $O$ and $T$, $W=9$ gives $U=9=W$. So $W=6$, $U=3$. Check: $867+867=1734$.

**Answer: (D) 3**

prompt: The areas of the faces of a rectangular box are $84\text{ cm}^2$, $70\text{ cm}^2$ and $30\text{ cm}^2$. The volume of the box in $\text{cm}^3$ is

solutions.title: Product of the areas
solutions.body:
Let the edges be $l,b,h$ with $lb=84$, $bh=70$, $hl=30$. Multiplying: $(lbh)^2=84\times70\times30=176\,400$, so $lbh=420$.

**Answer: (B) 420**

solutions.title: Find the edges
solutions.body:
$84=2^2\cdot3\cdot7$, $70=2\cdot5\cdot7$, $30=2\cdot3\cdot5$. The edge common to the 84 and 70 faces is 14, so the other edges are 6 and 5 ($14\times6=84$, $14\times5=70$, $6\times5=30$). Volume $14\times5\times6=420$.

**Answer: (B) 420**

prompt: The diameter of the big circle is divided into 5 parts. These five parts are the diameters of new circles as shown. If the circumference of the big circle is 30 cm, then the sum of the circumferences of the 5 smaller circles is

solutions.title: Circumference is proportional to diameter
solutions.body:
A circle's circumference is $\pi$ times its diameter. The five small diameters add up to the big diameter, so the five small circumferences add up to $\pi\times$(big diameter) $=30$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 30 cm**

prompt: You have 3 weights: 1 kg, 3 kg and 9 kg as well as an equal arm balance, as shown. How many different weight objects can you weigh with these three? [Remember the weights may be placed on either side]

solutions.title: List the possibilities
solutions.body:
Weights 1, 3, 9 can be placed on the same side as the object or on the opposite one, so every integer from 1 to 13 can be weighed: 1, 3, 9 directly; $4=1+3$; $10=1+9$; $12=3+9$; $13=1+3+9$; and with weights on the object's side: $2=3-1$, $8=9-1$, $6=9-3$, $7=9+1-3$, $11=9+3-1$, $5=9-3-1$. That is 13 values, 1 kg to 13 kg.

**Answer: (A) 13**

prompt: In the star, $\angle A+\angle B+\angle C+\angle D+\angle E+\angle F+\angle G=$

solutions.title: Seven triangles
solutions.body:
Join the centre O to the seven tips. The seven triangles, each with angle sum $180^\circ$, have a total of $7\times180^\circ=1260^\circ$. The angles at O make two full turns, $720^\circ$, and these are not part of the star's tips. Subtract: $1260^\circ-720^\circ=540^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $540^\circ$**

solutions.title: Use the heptagon
solutions.body:
Seven small triangles sit on the sides of the inner heptagon. Their angles total $7\times180^\circ$, of which the base angles are the exterior angles of the heptagon, which total $2\times360^\circ=4\times180^\circ$. What remains is $3\times180^\circ=540^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $540^\circ$**
